title: finding(console): the OAuth consent page names the requesting app by its raw client_id, because the console fetches a route the server does not serve
body:
Found by the `repo:www.objectos.ai` seat (objectstack-ai/objectstack#12224) on 2026-10-17, while staging www.objectos.ai#275. Measured on the published `@objectstack/cli` / `@objectstack/console` **17.7.0**. **Class a:** consent is the screen a user authorizes access on, and it does not say who is asking.

## What happens

- **The consent title.** A client registered through dynamic client registration with `client_name: "Claude Code"` reaches `/_console/oauth/consent`. The page reads **"hURqwHicPZUqDxuNgMQJksrzIXHCRmPR wants to access your account"**: the raw `client_id` instead of the registered name. At 1100 px the id also overflows its card.
- **The cause.** The console (17.7.0 dist, the consent component) calls `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth2/applications/{client_id}/public`, which answers **404**. The server's route is `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth2/public-client?client_id=…` (`auth-route-ledger.ts:178` at the tag), which answers 200 with `client_name` under the user's cookie.
- **The scope list.** The page lists `data:read`, `data:write` and `actions:execute` as raw strings, and only `openid`, `profile`, `email` and `offline_access` get human sentences. It is a read-only list with Deny and Authorize only, so there is no way to narrow the scopes.

## Why it matters

The consent screen is the only point at which a user decides to hand an agent access to their data. Showing an opaque id instead of the app's registered name defeats the user's ability to recognise what they are authorizing.

## Done looks like

- The consent page fetches the client's public metadata from the route the server serves, and titles the request with `client_name`, falling back to the id only if no name is registered.
- The three MCP scopes get human descriptions.
- A pin: register a client with a name, open consent, and the name is shown.

Related: the OAuth MCP delegator finding filed in the same pass.
